sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Certification and Security Auditing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage with a modern EU financial-regulation and commercial-law overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU-China Agreement for the mutual promotion and protection of investments (signed 25 November 1987; in force 4 July 1989)
Luxembourg-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital (signed 3 April 1996; in force 20 December 1996; amended by the 2004 and 2009 Protocols)
BLEU-Hong Kong Agreement for the promotion and protection of investments (1997)
Luxembourg participation in the OECD/G20 Multilateral Instrument (signed 7 June 2017; entered into force for Luxembourg 1 June 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 13 February 2018 and the Law of 25 March 2020 (implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE), as amended by the Law of 27 July 2024; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 February 2019 on RBE filing modalities; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT obligations; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 July 2018 on the RBE fee schedule.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / extract of the foreign commercial register in respect of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade or company register of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization where the country of origin is not a party to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the corporate resolutions authorizing subscription and capital contribution in the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction or certified corporate secretary copy, subsequently apostilled
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies of the general partner, limited partners and all ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of nationality or residence of each UBO, or certified true copy by a recognized professional followed by apostille
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney in favor of the Luxembourg-resident general partner or local representative for RCS and RBE filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the principal's country of origin, signed and sealed, apostilled where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Post-incorporation Luxembourg RCS extract and certificate of non-insolvency / non-registration of bankruptcy of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certification valid without apostille for Luxembourg banking use; apostille issued by the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs when lodged before foreign authorities

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-profiling of all UBOs, general partner, legal representatives, signatories and material commercial counterparties prior to incorporation and RBE declaration, comprising: (i) PEP screening as defined by Article 3(11) of the Law of 12 November 2004 (prominent public functions domestically or abroad, family members and known close associates); (ii) screening against the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated list under Council Regulations (EC) No 2580/2001 and (EU) No 881/2001, Luxembourg national asset-freezing measures administered by the Cellule de Renseignement Financier, and the OFAC SDN list in banking practice; (iii) adverse-media and high-risk-jurisdiction checks per FATF recommendations and CSSF Regulation 12-02; and (iv) enhanced due diligence with senior-management approval for any PEP, shell-bank connection or high-risk third-country nexus. Screening results must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years after termination of the business relationship in accordance with Article 5 of the Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic single platform at https://www.lbr.lu and https://www.rcs.lu; e-filing through the authenticated MyGuichet channel at https://guichet.public.lu.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS operates in French and filings may be made in French, German or Luxembourgish; a company name may be chosen in any language provided it is expressed in Latin-script alphabetic characters; any non-Latin script must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet with a sworn translation into French or German furnished to the RCS; the name must be distinguishable from all names already indexed in the RCS, must not be misleading as to the legal form, which must be identified as 'SCSp' or otherwise in a manner permitted for a registered partnership, and must comply with Article 1-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the special limited partnership.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying state sponsorship or public authority ('état', 'state', 'national', 'gouvernement', 'ministère', 'commune', 'municipal', 'Grand-Ducal') — require prior ministerial authorization

Regulated financial-sector terms ('banque', 'bank', 'assurance', 'insurance', 'réassurance', 'fonds d'investissement', 'investment fund', 'OPC', 'OPCVM', 'SICAV', 'société de gestion', 'PFS', 'professionnel du secteur financier') — reserved to CSSF-licensed entities
Terms suggesting a legal form other than the SCSp ('SA', 'S.à r.l.', 'SARL', 'SCA', 'SECA', 'société anonyme')
Terms implying a regulated profession without holding the required authorization ('expert-comptable', 'réviseur d'entreprises', 'avocat à la Cour', 'notaire', 'fiduciaire')
Trademark-protected or notoriously known corporate names creating a material passing-off risk under Article 1382 of the Luxembourg Civil Code
Names contrary to Luxembourg public order, public decency or international political sensitivities

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Title on Limited Partnerships — Articles 101-1 et seq., introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); supplemented by the Law of 12 July 2013 and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2013 on the RCS filing and RESA publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement / Articles of Limited Partnership (Contrat de société or Statuts de la société en commandite spéciale), filed for RCS registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement and no escrow/blocked-account rule. Contributions may be cash or in kind, and the amount is freely determined by the partners. The RCS registration fee is approximately EUR 75 (roughly USD 81) as published in the official tariff of Luxembourg Business Registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each signatory partner subscribes for the number of partnership interests set out in the Subscription Schedule, and that such contributions are made without application of minimum-capital escrow rules. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, as designated in the Partnership Agreement, with the Luxembourg Business Registers as the competent filing authority. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as managing general partner (associé gérant) with exclusive authority to represent the SCSp, and such manager is authorised to sign the RCS registration forms and all regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private parties; optional notary public in Luxembourg; no government approval at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership agreement (contrat de société) in French, German, or English, setting forth the firm name, registered office, object, partner contributions, allocation of profits, management powers of the general partner, and limitation of liability for limited partners. The agreement may be executed by private signature or notarial deed. Ensure each partner provides valid proof of identity and address; if a corporate body is a partner, produce certified articles and incumbency documentation.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all general and limited partners
Proof of address for each partner
If any partner is a legal entity: certified articles of association, certificate of good standing, board resolution authorising participation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the executing partner or notary identifies a formal defect, amend the agreement by private deed or re-pass before the notary; no state penalty if corrected before RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing and Data Capture
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) — online via MyGuichet.lu (LBR e-Filing) or in person at LBR, 2, avenue de la Liberté, L-1931 Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a MyGuichet.lu account and authenticate with LuxembourgKey. Complete the RCS-NEWCO electronic form, attach the scanned partnership agreement, and list all partners, managers, registered office, and object. Pay the RCS filing fee by bank card or direct debit. Validate the data using the LBR receipt. The RCS issues a provisional registration number and extracts the data for RESA.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, correct the flagged data directly in the MyGuichet draft and resubmit online within 15 business days; if the query concerns signature capacity, provide a fresh certified power of attorney or notarial legalisation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) publication service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS acceptance, the RCS automatically transmits the registration data to RESA for official publication. No separate manual filing is required. Monitor the RESA electronic gazette for the publication notice, obtain a certified copy of the RESA extract if needed for tax or banking purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or refused, contact the LBR helpdesk at info@lbr.lu, provide the RCS receipt, and request a manual publication order; any missing translation must be supplied within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Joint Management Centre for Social Security (CCSS) if employer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, submit the SCSp confirmation via MyGuichet to obtain a Luxembourg fiscal number and VAT identification number. Apply for VAT group treatment if applicable; the SCSp is tax transparent, but must file an annual tax return if any partner is a Luxembourg resident. If the partnership will have employees, register with the Joint Social Security Centre and subscribe to workplace accident insurance.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of the general partner
Power of attorney for tax representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT requires clarifications, file an amended tax registration through MyGuichet within ten days; if non-resident partners invoke double tax treaty relief, submit a certificate of residence from the partner's home tax authority to avoid withholding levy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UBO Registration and AEO Supply-Chain Audit Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Register; Ministry of Finance for AEO recognition (non-compulsory).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the UBO declaration with the RCS within one month of registration, identifying each natural person owning or controlling more than 25% of the SCSp. Establish the operational and security procedures required for the Authorized Economic Operator and supply-chain audit function: client KYC files, audit trail documentation, subcontractor due-diligence policies, and data-protection registers. Though AEO certification is elective for this consulting activity, maintain a compliance manual aligned with AEO security criteria.
required_dossiers: Organisational chart of ownership and control
Proof of professional indemnity insurance for audit services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UBO register query identifies missing beneficial-ownership data, amend the filing online within 30 days; for AEO voluntary application, remedy any security gap by submitting a corrective action plan to the Customs and Excise Administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Directorate-General for Industry and New Technologies (no operating permit required for ISIC 7020 management consultancy and compliance-audit services).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing operating permit required; only RCS commercial registration and, if applicable, municipal autorisation d'établissement for office-based services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA screening or full environmental impact report required for professional-services office activities under Category 4 of the grand-ducal EIA list.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or VOC process emissions. Office wastewater must comply with urban wastewater discharge standards under the law of 19 December 2008; electrical and electronic equipment waste must be handled under the WEEE regime; HVAC refrigerants must comply with EU F-gas Regulation (EU) 517/2014.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a municipal fire-safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) for the leased office premises; provide a structural load inspection certificate or building-code compliance certificate from the landlord for the professional workplace; obtain an occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) covering workstations, emergency exits, and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for value added tax and registration duties. Central digital portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities not established in Luxembourg but conducting taxable supplies must register for VAT via the AEDT using form 645 (VAT registration application), submitted through MyGuichet or by an appointed Luxembourg tax representative, attaching constitutional documents, proof of foreign TIN, and evidence of economic activity. Resident entities receive a Luxembourg national business registration number (matricule) from the Luxembourg Business Registers, which serves as the direct tax TIN; VAT numbers are issued in the format LU0000000000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: A Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) has no separate legal personality and is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes. As an unincorporated partnership, it is not a CIT taxpayer; partners are taxed on their share of income. For VAT, the SCSp may still be a taxable person when pursuing an independent economic activity above applicable turnover thresholds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime. The SCSp is mandatorily tax-transparent and cannot elect entity-level taxation. Specific elections include: (i) waiver of the small-business VAT exemption (option for taxation), (ii) formation of a VAT grouping (assujetti unique) subject to conditions, and (iii) anti-hybrid notifications and consistency statements under ATAD and Luxembourg domestic implementation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), implemented under the Luxembourg VAT Code (Loi TVA) and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover of supplies for small-business exemption); separate thresholds apply to intra-EU distance sales (EUR 10,000) and to intra-EU acquisitions of goods by non-established entities, above which compulsory Luxembourg VAT registration is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory live e-invoice clearance regime exists in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is permitted and accepted (Factur-X, PEPPOL) with mandatory e-invoicing for public sector contracts. VAT reporting is performed through periodic returns (forms 1, 3, 5, 6) filed electronically via MyGuichet; no transaction-level reporting mandate applies outside of Intrastat and EU VAT reporting rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods dispatched or transported to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT, including direct exports, export indirect exports, and services physically or economically linked to export goods, provided the supplier holds documentary evidence establishing the exit of goods from the EU and the identity/relation of the purchaser. Intra-EU dispatches to VAT-registered counterparties may also be zero-rated with a valid VAT ID.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / electronic customs declaration)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR or other transport contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank receipt proving receipt of consideration
Transport documents showing physical departure from EU territory
Proof of EU customs exit confirmation (ECS / simplified declaration records)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg customs and direct tax authorities can retrospectively verify export documentation through AEO security audits and cross-checks with ECS exit data. Missing or inadequate evidence invalidates the 0% rate and triggers a reassessment at 17% VAT, plus late-payment interest. Tax penalties for negligent under-declaration range up to 10% of the corrected tax; fraudulent export claims may trigger penalties up to 100% of evaded VAT, criminal fines up to EUR 500,000, and/or custodial penalties, with clawbacks extending over a five-year limitation period (ten years for fraud).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the European Central Bank for Eurosystem operations; regulatory oversight of payment institutions and EMI licensing by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates as part of the euro area with full and unrestricted convertibility on both capital and current account transactions. Profit remittances, dividends, partnership distributions, and loan repayments to non-residents are freely permitted without exchange control authorization or prior approval, subject only to standard EU anti-money laundering, sanctions, beneficial ownership disclosure, and tax compliance documentation. No material hurdles exist for the SCSp, which is treated as a tax-transparent partnership for direct tax purposes when not subject to corporate income tax in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no Luxembourg statutory export proceeds surrender requirements, mandatory conversion ratios, or prescribed timelines for repatriating or converting export receipts into euro. Luxembourg does not maintain reserves-related exchange controls; all euro-denominated and foreign-currency export proceeds may be held, converted, or disbursed freely. Nevertheless, commercial compliance under the EU Customs Code and the Authorized Economic Operator security audit regime requires proper trade transaction documentation, customs valuation reporting, and retained records for a minimum of ten years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and EU passporting EMIs e.g. Wirecard Alternative, TransactPro, or niche global transfer providers operating under an EU passport via a Luxembourg branch or agent. Legal constraints: Non-EEA digital only EMIs cannot serve as the primary clearing and settlement bank for an AEO supply-chain audit engagement because statutory partner drawdown and escrowed capital mechanics require a fully regulated Luxembourg or EU-authorised deposit-taking credit institution or authorized payment/e-money institution. Use of non-EU offshore EMIs is restricted to ancillary high-value cross-border payroll or minor vendor disbursements, not core treasury accounts. Core accounts must remain at a CSSF-supervised bank or a sanctioned EU credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding may be permitted in Luxembourg through advanced video identification and digital signature processes where the bank and client complete a secure interview under CSSF AML Circular 12/544 as amended and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2020. However, virtually all tier-1 Luxembourg commercial banks will nonetheless require at least one physical appearance of the general partner, the ultimate beneficial owner, or an authorised statutory representative at the bank's registered office in Luxembourg for the first onboarding meeting, especially because an SCSp is a non-trading partnership with no inherent legal personality under Luxembourg law. The bank will request a board resolution or partnership authority document confirming the physical signatory mandate. Where the general partner is a corporate entity, the bank may also require economic substance documentation and a physical address for the entity in Luxembourg; a remote-only opening is generally unavailable to first-time non-resident SCSp structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident owner situs and majority non-tax-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Folder containing: certified passport copies, proof of address not older than three months, FATCA and CRS self-certification forms, a full transparency organigram showing the direct and indirect ownership chain, an up-to-date Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE) filing, the limited partnership agreement, a signed private placement memorandum, and the annual audited financial statements or certified management accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp classification causing uncertain commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-part substance file: (1) Luxembourg general partner appointment deed; (2) certificate of economic activity or a copy of the AEO auditor commercial contract; (3) lease or domiciliation agreement in Luxembourg; (4) monthly payroll records of local staff or a management agreement with a Luxembourg operator; (5) bank statements showing active operational transactions and clearing; (6) a written explanation from the tax advisor addressing the electable transparency status and absence of CIT exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrowed capital or liquidation-only distribution mechanics perceived as attempted money-laundering layering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive capital deployment schedule, signed capital commitments, a copy of the escrow or bank guarantee arrangement, underlying AEO audit invoices and trade documents, and a sworn declaration confirming the source of assets is derived from regulated inbound commercial contracts rather than shell financing or third-party proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire receipts from high-friction jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bankable trade verification packet: issued commercial invoice, packing list, customs declaration, AEO or dual-runner certification, carrier bill of lading / airway bill, letter of instruction from the client, and ISO 20022 purpose-of-payment codes validated by the counterparty bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound SWIFT flows carrying high-value professional consulting fees without underlying payroll / VAT trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciliation binder matching each invoice to the payment mandate, the VAT summary declaration and Luxembourg reverse-charge VAT treatment where applicable, timesheets / audit sign-off sheets, and a copy of the customs or trade-security report demonstrating the substantive supply-chain audit service.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital contributions for the SCSp must be routed via the euro-area SEPA channel for euro wires (mandatory use of IBAN and BIC) or, for non-euro foreign currency, via SWIFT MT103 with clear instructing messages. Standard purpose codes to prevent false classification: for equity subscription use ISO 20022 Purpose Code 'EQUI' (Equity participation); for shareholder loan use 'LOAN'; and for escrowed capital injection into the AEO audit project use 'CNCE' (Cash management and transfer services or commercial settlement), 'TRADE' (Trade transaction), or 'COMC' (Commercial contract). Banks will require a board or partner resolution, an undertaking to comply with BCL statistics and balance-of-payment reporting if the counterparty is a regulated entity, and the source-of-funds verification package described above. Inbound funds should never be routed to a personal account; they must settle directly on the SCSp's dedicated capital escrow or operational account at a CSSF-supervised bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for AEO supply-chain audit deliverables should be drawn from the operational account via SWIFT MT103 for international non-euro beneficiaries and SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-area payments. For substantial customs-related trade flows, the principal may use a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary usance LC) where the Luxembourg bank endorses the eligible audit invoice, AEO certificate, and security pre-clearance evidence as presentation documents. Where counterparties require additional assurance, the bank may issue an SBLC (standby letter of credit) on the basis of the SCSp's audited capital position. Payment instructions must be matched against the invoice, the customs duty declaration, and the bank's internal AML watchlist screening. All outbound disbursements must carry explicit reference numbers and bank-approved payment purpose codes, typically 'TRADE', 'COMM', 'PROF', or 'CONS' depending on the commercial nature of the settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards with a CSSF-supervised credit institution for non-euro AEO contract settlements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the Lugated counterparty currency is subject to local convertibility restrictions
Cross-currency swaps used solely for treasury balance-sheet matching between the SCSp's EUR base and the trade disbursement currency
Plain-vanilla FX call and put options for hedging definable supply-chain audit invoice receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) – Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each calendar year, confirming data as at 31 December of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 125,000 per the UBO Law of 13 January 2019; publication of non-compliance; possible imprisonment of responsible officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the RCSL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end), where the SCSp meets mandatory filing thresholds; otherwise statutory exemption applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive fine (astreinte) of EUR 500 per day of delay, capped at EUR 25,000; additional civil liability of general partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for partnerships (composite return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des Contributions Directes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., FY 2024 return due 31 December 2025), extendible to 30 June 2026 upon authorized accountant request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine up to EUR 5,000; default interest at 3.2% per annum; potential tax assessment based on estimated income.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required for Luxembourg SCSp if the partnership exceeds any two of the three size criteria: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net revenue EUR 8.8 million, average headcount 50; or if all general partners are limited liability entities, irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, as amended) aligned with EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SCSp must confirm annually through the LBR bePortail that the registered ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) details remain accurate as at 31 December. Any ownership transfer or change in control must be filed with the RCSL within 30 days of occurrence. The annual confirmation is obligatory even in the absence of any shareholding transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – USD 750 (typical annual fee for registered office/agent in Luxembourg)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 12,000 (typical audit fee for a small/medium SCSp)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg-City combined rate for corporate partners: 17% CIT (LIR Art. 174) + 1.19% solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT) + 6.75% municipal business tax (rate varies by commune). The SCSp itself is fiscally transparent; CIT is assessed at partner level on allocated profit shares.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (LIR Art. 166/115): 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (≥10% interest or ≥EUR 1.2M acquisition cost; 12-month holding). IP box (LIR Art. 50ter): 80% exemption of qualifying IP-derived income. Notional Interest Deduction (LIR Art. 168quater): deduction of the AAA-bond-derived rate on qualifying increases in equity capital. 20% R&D tax credit on qualifying research expenditures. No traditional tax-holiday regime; SCSp pass-through preserves incentive eligibility for partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (Luxembourg LIR Art. 110 grants indefinite business-loss carry-forward; no statutory 5-year cap, but continuity of the same commercial activity and absence of an abusive ownership change are conditions).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 100 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités / société de personnes) filed electronically via the Luxembourg Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) e-filing portal on MyGuichet.lu, authenticated by LuxTrust digital certificate; accompanying annexes include the income-allocation schedule for the fiscally transparent SCSp.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The transparent SCSp files one partnership-level declaration per fiscal year; each partner reports its allocable share in its own annual CIT/income-tax return. Corporate partners must remit quarterly provisional CIT instalments (March, June, September, December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual declaration must be filed by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., a year ending 31 December 2024 is due 31 December 2025). The ACD may grant extensions upon reasoned written request; no extension postpones a partner's obligation to pay assessed instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, Luxembourg RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax file number (N° matricule), registered office, general partner details, and fiscal year-end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners must be listed by name, foreign tax identification number, country of tax residence, and profit-sharing ratio; the declaration must clearly state the absence of a Luxembourg permanent establishment unless the AEO audit activity is performed through Luxembourg personnel.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit of the SCSp adjusted to Luxembourg tax basis: disallowed expenses added back, exempt participation income and IP-box deductions removed, and ATAD interest-limitation adjustments applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg-source business assets is taxable for non-resident partners; the partnership declaration must segregate Luxembourg-PE income from foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the taxable result among the general partner and limited partners in accordance with the SCSp partnership agreement and their respective capital accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach an extract of the partnership agreement, the share percentages, and each non-resident partner's tax-residency certificate; state the applicable double-tax-treaty article for elimination of Luxembourg taxation if no PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 400 – Impôt commercial communal (Municipal Business Tax Base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Communal trade-tax base calculated from the CIT income base with statutory add-backs (typically 50% of interest and 70% of royalty expenses) and deductibility of the municipal business tax itself.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Relevant only where the SCSp carries on a permanent commercial or professional activity in Luxembourg; non-resident partners are not severally liable for the communal trade tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax plus default interest at 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.) on unpaid tax. The ACD may issue a default assessment (taxation d'office) where no declaration is filed or records are inadequate. Intentional concealment or false declarations attract surcharges of up to 100% of the evaded tax and criminal fines up to EUR 150,000; recidivism doubles the sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (LIR Art. 146). Because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, profit distributions by the SCSp are not classified as dividends for Luxembourg tax purposes: no WHT is withheld at the partnership level, and partners are taxed through their annual assessment. Where a corporate partner would have qualified for the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive regime, qualifying outbound dividends from a Luxembourg corporate entity benefit from 0% WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the beneficial-owner partner must provide a current Luxembourg Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) plus a statement of beneficial ownership to the Luxembourg paying entity before payment; the paying agent then applies the treaty rate at source. If excess tax has already been withheld, a refund claim (demande en remboursement) must be filed with the ACD within the statutory limitation period (generally 5 years), supported by the TRC, dividend voucher, and treaty article analysis. For the SCSp, the transparent structure requires a partner-level TRC rather than an SCSp-level one.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no domestic withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments. Under EU Directive 2003/49/EC, associated EU companies benefit from 0% WHT on cross-border interest and royalties. DTA variations: interest typically 0–15%, royalties 0–10%, depending on the treaty counterparty. Payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions may be recharacterized or subjected to anti-abuse denial of the exemption, resulting in 15% WHT exposure for dividend-like income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue is the statutory threshold for CbC Report and Master File obligations under the Luxembourg implementation of EU Directive 2016/881 (DAC4). Local File / contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation must be maintained by a Luxembourg taxpayer for all significant cross-border controlled transactions; in administrative practice, the ACD expects a Local File where annual related-party flows exceed approximately EUR 1,000,000 in aggregate or where intercompany service fees exceed EUR 100,000 per category, and the documentation must be submitted upon request within 30 days. Form 100's transfer-pricing annex must disclose intercompany transactions in all materially affected categories.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate an offshore-style Economic Substance Regulation, but economic substance is enforced through the General Anti-Abuse Rule (LIR Art. 6 and the Abgabenordnung Art. 6 AAbL), the ATAD-implemented interest-limitation rule (LIR Art. 168quater), the MLI principal-purpose test for treaty benefits, and DAC6 disclosure rules. The SCSp undertaking AEO supply-chain security audits must demonstrate real commercial substance in Luxembourg: a local registered office, senior management functions performed in Luxembourg, qualified staff conducting audit work, and genuine decision-making on invoices and contracts. A shell-like SCSp without such substance risks recharacterization, denial of treaty relief, 0% WHT denial, and retrospective allocation of profits to the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false or incomplete Luxembourg tax declaration: omission of AEO audit revenue, inclusion of fictitious subcontracted expenses, use of backdated invoices, or deliberate under-declaration of partner profit shares.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of tax at the ACD's discretion plus monthly default interest of 0.6%; concealment surcharge of up to 100% of the evaded tax; late-filing surcharge of 10%. Criminal conviction for tax fraud after 1 January 2023: fine of EUR 10,000 to EUR 500,000 and/or imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, graduated by the amount of tax evaded and whether the offense was committed as part of an organized group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner who sign or cause the filing of a false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and penalties under the Luxembourg Companies Law (Law of 10 August 1915, Art. 59); criminal personal exposure includes fines, imprisonment, publication of the conviction, and an exit ban (interdiction de sortie du territoire) pending resolution of the criminal case.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a letterbox entity without Luxembourg substance, with a nominee general partner, passive flow-through of income, and interposition solely to obtain treaty benefits or the EU 0% WHT regime on interest, royalties, or dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under LIR Art. 6 and the OECD/MLI principal-purpose test; denial of treaty benefits and statutory exemptions; retrospective taxation of the true beneficial owner; penalty surcharge of 10% plus 0.6% monthly interest on the reassessed amount; potential ATAD exit-tax charge on migration of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate veil is pierced for abuse or fraud, the general partner and directing officers face personal civil liability for the unpaid corporate tax plus punitive surcharges; criminal tax-fraud charges attach if the artificial arrangement is used to conceal taxable income, carrying prison terms and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing Authorized Economic Operator security audits while failing to maintain mandatory customs-security audit files, client due-diligence records, or suspicious-transaction reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF); accepting proceeds of tax evasion or predicate offenses through the SCSp's payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of AEO certification by the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 in serious AML cases and debarment from tender/supply-chain mandates; criminal AML sanctions under the Luxembourg amended law of 12 November 2004 include fines of up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment of 1 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are personally liable for AML compliance failures; deliberate non-reporting triggers personal criminal fines and imprisonment and cannot be indemnified by the partnership; customs authorities may impose individual travel bans and directors may be barred from exercising managerial functions in regulated supply-chain roles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or produce contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation upon ACD request; pricing AEO audit and consulting intercompany fees at non-arm's-length margins; maintaining no substance to support the allocation of profits to the Luxembourg SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under LIR Art. 56, the ACD will make a primary upward adjustment to the arm's-length result, with secondary adjustment and re-allocation of profits to the European or non-resident related party; 0.6% monthly interest applies from the original due date; a documentation-default penalty of 10% of the adjusted tax may be imposed; double-taxation relief through MAP is denied where documentation is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for the accounting and filing obligations bear personal civil liability for penalties arising from non-documentation; in a criminal tax-evasion context, the deliberate absence of TP documentation is treated as circumstantial evidence of intent, exposing directors to personal fines and imprisonment; the Luxembourg tax administration may also seek personal recovery from directors who signed tax returns based on fabricated transfer-pricing data.
